label: Pipeline: the latest push to all green
means: Minutes from the latest pull request push to every check passing; the drawing shows each step's latest run
goal_source: the ten-minute build (Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained, 2nd edition, 2004; Martin Fowler, Continuous Integration, 2024-01-18) and DORA's continuous integration capability (read 2026-11-03): tests take an upper limit of about 10 minutes
source: latest: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs per head SHA, the latest pull request head that went all green; each stage's latest run of the last 20 per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them), with its pass rate over those 20; review and deploy stages from the latest of the last 20 merged pull requests; stages from .claude/settings.json, the git hooks in params.hooks_dir, .github/workflows and params.stages

stages.label: Review and merge
stages.runs: A person reviews the pull request, then merges it; timed from all checks green to the merge
stages.file: branch rules on the default branch

label: Slowest workflow, its latest real run
means: Minutes the slowest workflow took the last time it did real work; runs that skip their work are left out
goal_source: the ten-minute build (Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained, 2nd edition, 2004; Martin Fowler, Continuous Integration, 2024-01-18; DORA's continuous integration capability, read 2026-11-03): workflows run side by side, so the slowest one sets the build time
source: latest: GraphQL check runs and steps of the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them), each workflow's latest run that did real work

label: Minutes the default branch is red
means: How long a workflow on the default branch has been failing, right now; 0 when every one passed last; lower is better
goal_source: DORA's continuous integration capability (read 2026-11-03): a build that cannot be fixed in a few minutes has its change reverted; Martin Fowler, Continuous Integration (2024-01-18): fix broken builds immediately; template goal: 10 minutes, one build's length
source: state: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, each workflow's runs on a push to the default branch: when its latest decided run failed, red from the end of the first failure after its latest success

label: Runner dollars at list price, the latest merged PR
means: Runner dollars the CI runs of the latest merged pull request cost; small, right-first-time changes cost less
goal_source: template goal: 60 runner minutes a merged pull request, near 100, priced at GitHub's standard Linux 2-core rate of $0.006 a minute (GitHub docs, Actions runner pricing, read 2026-11-03): 60 x $0.006 = $0.36, 100 x $0.006 = $0.60
source: latest: the latest of the last 20 merged pull requests (when it opened before the runs read cover every workflow, or only runs its merge started are still going, the newest before it that can be priced, each one passed over named in the note; could_not_check when none can, or a branch run of it is still going); its runs (its branch's pull_request runs and its merge commit's push runs, gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs), each priced from its own jobs (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most: each job's billed minutes, rounded up, times its runs-on label's list rate: ubuntu-slim $0.002, Linux 2-core x64 $0.006, Linux 2-core arm64 $0.005, Windows $0.010, macOS 3 or 4-core $0.062 a minute, GitHub docs, Actions runner pricing, read 2026-11-03)

label: Runner minutes per issue, the latest fix
means: Billed runner minutes the CI runs of the latest pull request that closed an issue took, per issue it closed
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-03): a fix uses no more runner time than a merged pull request, 60 billed runner minutes, near 100, as for ci.latest_pr_dollars
source: latest: the latest merged pull request that closed an issue (GraphQL closingIssuesReferences; when it opened before the runs read cover every workflow, or only runs its merge started are still going, the newest such one before it that can be priced, each one passed over named in the note; could_not_check when none can, or a branch run of it is still going); its runs (gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs), each job's billed minutes from its own jobs (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most, rounded up to the minute), summed and divided by the issues it closed

label: Runner minutes per pull request, the latest card
means: Billed runner minutes the CI runs took, per merged pull request of the card most recently marked done
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-04): a card's pull requests use no more runner time than a merged pull request, 60 billed runner minutes, near 100, as for ci.latest_pr_dollars
source: latest: the board named by github.json's params.project_title (gh api graphql, projectsV2): of the five cards most recently moved to the done column that link merged pull requests, the newest whose runs can be priced (could_not_check when none can: each opened before the runs read cover every workflow, or has a run still going); their runs (gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs) and REST jobs' billed runner minutes (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most, rounded up to the minute), summed and divided by those pull requests

label: Runner minutes, the latest security scans
means: Billed runner minutes the latest run of each security scan workflow took; the scans still run on every change
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-03): the scans on one change bill at most 5 runner minutes, half the ten-minute build (Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained, 2nd edition, 2004)
source: latest: gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs (each job's billed minutes, rounded up) for each workflow whose name matches params.security_workflows: the repo's own, its latest run that did real work of the newest 10 of its last 20 runs (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them); GitHub's dynamic ones such as CodeQL default setup, their latest passed run; summed. GitHub's dynamic CodeQL - Code Quality run is left out: code.quality_scan_minutes reads it

label: Runner minutes, the latest Code Quality scan
means: Billed runner minutes the latest passed run of GitHub's Code Quality scan took; lower is better
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-13): the Code Quality scan on one change bills at most 5 runner minutes, as the security scans do, half the ten-minute build (Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained, 2nd edition, 2004)
source: latest: gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs (each job's billed minutes, rounded up) for GitHub's dynamic workflow named CodeQL - Code Quality, its latest passed run, read with the security scans, so no extra request

label: Runs that find nothing to do
means: Share of runs that start a runner only to skip their work because nothing they check changed; each still bills
goal_source: template goal: at most one run in four starts a runner only to skip its work
source: GraphQL check runs and steps (step conclusions) of the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median and a p90, few enough that new runs replace them); weighted by each workflow and event's runs since the start of the shortest full list of 100

label: Runner minutes, the latest push to the default branch
means: Billed runner minutes the CI runs of the latest commit pushed to the default branch took, summed over its workflows
goal_source: GitHub docs, GitHub Actions billing (read 2026-11-10): each job bills its minutes rounded up, so every workflow a push starts bills at least one; template goal (2026-11-10): the runs one push starts bill at most the ten-minute build (Martin Fowler, Continuous Integration, 2024-01-18), near 20
source: latest: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, the push runs of the latest commit on the default branch whose runs all ended (the run collecting and any push with a run still going passed over, up to 5, each named in the note); their REST jobs (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most): each job's billed minutes, rounded up, summed

label: Triggers that skip work when nothing changed
means: Share of pull request and push triggers that skip their work when no file they check changed; a skipped run bills less
goal_source: GitHub docs, Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions: on.<push|pull_request>.paths and paths-ignore skip a run when no matching file changed; template goal: at most one trigger in five runs its work on every change
source: state: .github/workflows, each pull_request and push to main trigger: a paths or paths-ignore filter, a job whose if reads a needs.*.outputs value (a changes job), or a job calling ci-standard.yml with paths

label: Checks that failed, then passed on the same commit
means: Share of workflow checks on one commit that failed and later passed with no change to the code
goal_source: template goal: below the 1.5% of test runs that Google reported flaky (Google Testing Blog, Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them, 2016)
source: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median and a p90, few enough that new runs replace them), and runs/{id}/attempts/1 for every rerun that passed; a later pass counts on a push, and on a pull request only as a rerun

label: npm installs that reused the cache
means: Share of npm installs in CI that restored the saved package cache instead of downloading every package again
goal_source: GitHub docs, Caching dependencies to speed up workflows; template goal: nine npm installs in ten restore the cache
source: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs (setup-node's npm cache line, newest 12 jobs of the last 20 runs per workflow)

label: Job wait for a runner
means: Seconds a job waits between being queued and starting on a runner, at the 90th percentile; lower is better
goal_source: GitHub docs, Actions metrics (read 2026-11-10): the performance view reports average queue time and sets no number; template goal: nine jobs in ten start within 30 seconds, near 60
source: last 10 completed runs per workflow, the queue sample the CI tab already reads (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs): each job's started_at less created_at

label: Workflow runs that failed
means: Share of workflow runs that failed, of those that passed or failed; each failure costs a fix and another run
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-11): no first-party source sets a number; one run in ten, near one in five. GitHub docs, About GitHub Actions metrics (read 2026-11-11) lists failure rates as a key indicator and sets none. Cancelled and skipped runs give no verdict, so they are left out
source: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them): runs that ended failure, timed_out or startup_failure, over those that passed or failed, on any event

label: Minutes that bought nothing
means: Share of billed minutes on runs cancelled, timed out or failed after merge; a failed pull request check is not waste
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-10): no first-party source sets a number; a tenth, near a fifth. GitHub docs, About GitHub Actions metrics (read 2026-11-10) reports failure rate and sets none. A failure on a pull request is the check working, so only cancelled, timed-out and post-merge failures count; a merge queue failure is the check working too
source: GraphQL check runs of the last 20 runs per workflow: each job's minutes rounded up as GitHub bills them, summed for runs that ended cancelled, timed_out or startup_failure, or failed outside a pull request or merge queue, over all

label: Runner list price per billed minute
means: Cents a billed runner minute costs at list price; lighter jobs on the 1-core ubuntu-slim runner bring it down
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-10): half the billed minutes on ubuntu-slim, priced from GitHub docs, Actions runner pricing (read 2026-11-10): ubuntu-slim 0.2 cents and Linux 2-core 0.6 cents a minute, (0.2 + 0.6) / 2 = 0.4; near 0.6, every minute on the 2-core rate
source: last 10 completed runs per workflow, the queue sample the Actions tab already reads (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs): each job's billed minutes, rounded up, times its runs-on label's list rate (RUNNER_RATES), over the minutes; could_not_check when a job ran on a runner with no list price

label: GitHub API left this hour
means: Share of the hourly GitHub API quota still unused, REST or GraphQL, whichever is lower; every session shares it
goal_source: goal set from readings (2026-11-11): the account's login had 52.8% of its REST requests left right after an org collect (2,638 of 5,000, 2026-11-10 18:23 UTC) and 95.7% at a quiet hour (GraphQL 4,783 of 5,000, 2026-11-11 16:23 UTC); a goal of half left keeps a full collect's room, near a fifth
source: latest: gh api rate_limit (counts against no limit), each bucket's remaining over its limit, read with the token the run holds: latest.json the CI run's, local.json the account's login

label: GitHub requests per pull request run
means: Requests the workflow token spent live in the latest green pull request run of pages.yml; a replayed read costs none
goal_source: goal from issue #38 (2026-11-12); near is the 765 a pull request run spent before replay (run 43307560596's quota lines). The workflow token reports limit 5000 an hour (gh api rate_limit in runs 43307560596 and 43355450949)
source: latest: gh api actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs (green pull_request runs from this repo), the newest one's jobs and their check-run annotations: each job's GitHub requests notice from quality/gh-replay.mjs, live REST plus GraphQL, summed
